domain_note: Authenticated bytes are the ASCII domain, one NUL byte, then the canonical payload with signature or mac removed.
authenticator_note: Cases marked authenticator=valid must pass cryptographic verification so the semantic rule under test is actually reached. Cases marked invalid fail verification itself.
warning: Seeds below are published test values and must never sign anything real.
key_naming_note: signing_key_seed_hex and authority_receipt_seed_hex are the same key: the receipt authority's. Both names are published because the first is this corpus's convention for whichever key signs the artifact, and the second names its purpose. A previous revision had them differ, so signing_key_seed_hex named a key that did not sign the valid case -- a trap for anyone following the convention.
rejection_integrity_note: Each rejection case must differ from the valid case in the field or authenticator its name identifies. A regeneration that re-signs every case whose authenticator is 'valid' erases exactly these defects -- 'valid' marks a case that must verify so the semantic rule is reached, not a case that is correct.
range_digest_note: sha256 over the concatenation of the raw 32-byte chain_row_digest values for from_seq..to_seq in ascending local_seq order, with no separators and no hex encoding. The valid case receipts local_seq 12 from delivery-envelope.json so an independent implementation can reproduce the range rather than trusting hidden generator state.

cases.name: valid
cases.note: Canonical bytes, range digest and signature independently reproduce under the receipt key.

cases.name: signed_with_epoch_key
cases.note: Identical content to the valid case, signed with the epoch authority's key. Purpose separation is the rule under test: an epoch key cannot receipt a range.

cases.name: non_contiguous_range
cases.note: Correctly signed by the receipt key, claiming 9 to 12 while the range digest covers only 12. A receipt must not span a local_seq the authority did not accept.
